evals.name: check-reports-lint-and-format-passes-separately
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, shellcheck for the lint pass, shfmt for the format pass, the .editorconfig shell opt-in, .shellcheckrc discovery, the bash_format_enabled toggle, hook registration, and project scope — with one remediation line per FAIL and no file modified.
expectations: Reports the lint pass (shellcheck) and the format pass (shfmt) as two independent rows rather than one combined formatter verdict
Reports missing jq as FAIL and states the consequence: the hook skips with a visible once-per-session notice instead of running either pass
Reports .shellcheckrc absence as INFO, not FAIL, because ShellCheck applies its own defaults when it discovers none
Modifies nothing during check and reports the effective bash_format_enabled value rather than parsing settings files for hook registration

evals.name: bare-star-editorconfig-section-is-not-the-shell-opt-in
evals.prompt:
/bash-format:setup check

We do have an .editorconfig at the repo root, but the only section in it is [*] with end_of_line and charset. Why is nothing being formatted?
evals.expected_output: States that a bare [*] catch-all is NOT the shell opt-in — the opt-in is a section naming shell files ([*.sh], [*.bash], [*.{sh,bash}], or a path-prefixed form) — so the format pass is inert by design, which is a configuration answer rather than a defect to repair.
expectations: Says a bare [*] catch-all does not count as the opt-in, and neither does a path-only section such as [scripts/**]
Classifies the un-opted-in format pass as INFO (inert by design), not FAIL, and does not offer to repair it
States the consequence the hook's own logic produces: shell files are left unformatted rather than rewritten to shfmt's built-in defaults
Downgrades a missing shfmt to INFO in this state instead of calling it a defect

evals.name: never-writes-repo-config-or-installs-packages
evals.prompt:
/bash-format:setup apply

shellcheck and shfmt are both missing and we have no shell section in .editorconfig. Just fix all of it for me.
evals.expected_output: Declines to install shellcheck or shfmt and declines to write the repository's .editorconfig or .shellcheckrc; prints the install guidance and explains that .editorconfig is cross-cutting so the edit belongs to the consumer.
expectations: Does not run any system package manager — install guidance is printed for the reader to run
Does not write .editorconfig or .shellcheckrc, and gives the reason: .editorconfig governs every editor and tool in the repo, so the choice is the consumer's
Does not write Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache
Names the exact section forms that would opt the repo in ([*.sh], [*.bash], [*.{sh,bash}]) without adding them

evals.name: green-check-is-not-every-shell-edit-covered
evals.prompt:
/bash-format:setup check

Everything came back green last time — so every .sh file I touch anywhere gets linted and formatted, right?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the unqualified reading: when CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set, the hook acts only on shell files inside it, so a .sh or .bash file written to a temp or scratchpad directory is silently skipped with no lint, no format, and no notice.
expectations: Never reports an unqualified "fully operational" — the all-green result is stated with the project-scope caveat attached
States that an out-of-project shell edit is skipped silently, producing no notice of any kind
Notes that the OS temp tree counts as outside even when it sits under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, unless the project root itself lives under temp
States the opposite case: when CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset the membership guard is skipped and any existing edited file is processed

evals.name: second-apply-reports-already-configured
evals.prompt:
/bash-format:setup apply

I ran this ten minutes ago and everything passed. Run it again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and changes nothing on the second pass.
expectations: Runs check before offering any remediation, even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write on the second run
Does not prompt interactively — the action was given in the invocation
Does not re-issue install guidance for prerequisites that now pass

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/bash-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install bash-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config bash_format_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (verified on Claude Code 2.1.240), explicitly rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config bash_format_enabled=false` rerun as the headless route, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option to its manifest default
Carries the CLI version the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim was verified on — the literal 2.1.240 — and scopes it to a non-sensitive option at user scope

Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory, or the write lands at a scope that does not load
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect
